opennyai_summary.13_August_2024__facts:
2.  This application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashing of the entire proceedings, including charge-sheet dated 04.06.2022 and cognizance/summoning order dated 18.01.2023, of criminal case No. 450 of 2023, arising out of case crime no. 132 of 2021, under Section 376 IPC, P.S. Rajpur,
District Kanpur Dehat, pending in the court of C.J.M., Kanpur Dehat, on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.
opennyai_summary.13_August_2024__arguments:
Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 /informant has concurred with the arguments of learned counsel for the applicants and submitted that both the parties have amicably settled the dispute and compromised the matter and the informant does not want to proceed with the case pending before the trial court and the impugned proceedings may be quashed, as no useful purpose would be served by exhausting remedy of trial.
5. Learned A.G.A. has no objection if parties compromise the matter.
opennyai_summary.13_August_2024__ANALYSIS:
7. In the instant case, perusal of record shows that charge-sheet has been submitted against the applicant under Section 376 IPC.
It may be stated that generally the proceedings of serious offences like that of rape cannot be quashed on the basis of compromise between the parties.
However, in the instant case perusal of record shows that informant was a major girl and in her statement, recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she has inter-alia stated that she as well as applicant used to like each other and her family was ready for her marriage with applicant.
She has stated that applicant has established physical relations with her on pretext of marriage but later on the family members of applicant have refused for his marriage with informant and thereafter they have married with each other in a temple but the family members of applicant were not ready to accept the same and due to these reasons, she has lodged this case.
Prima facie, it appears a case of breach of promise of marriage and no case under Section 376 IPC is made out.
There is nothing to indicate that parties have any criminal antecedents.
Considering the law laid down in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others, AIR 2019 SC 1296 and the facts of the matter, it would be in the interest of justice that the impugned proceedings be quashed, as the continuance of the same would be nothing but wastage of time of Court.
opennyai_summary.13_August_2024__decision:
8. In view of the aforesaid, the impugned charge-sheet/cognizance-summoning order and entire proceedings of the aforesaid criminal case against applicant Shivam Singh are, hereby, quashed.
9. The application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed.
